finding: The AUA summary groups recommendations of different strengths and labels only buccal versus lingual graft equivalence. State the strength beside each operative rule so an Expert Opinion is not read as Grade A evidence.
evidence: AUA 2023 unabridged full text, statements 18b, 19a, 19b and 32, opened at reports/audit-v2/sources-local/aua-urethral-stricture-2023-unabridged.txt; official source https://www.auanet.org/documents/Guidelines/Archive/Urethral%20Stricture%20Disease%20Unabridged%20FINAL%20060923.pdf. Oral mucosa first-choice is Expert Opinion; avoiding genital skin in LS is Strong/Grade B; PU for patients at high risk of reconstruction failure is Expert Opinion; buccal/lingual equivalence is Strong/Grade A.

edit.old: The AUA 2023 guideline anchors three of its most consequential rules: oral mucosa is the first-choice graft, avoid genital skin in lichen sclerosus, and perineal urethrostomy is a legitimate long-term option for high-risk patients.<sup>[[2]](#ref2)</sup>
edit.new: The AUA 2023 guideline names oral mucosa as the first-choice graft (Expert Opinion), advises against genital skin in lichen sclerosus (Strong Recommendation; Grade B), and advises offering perineal urethrostomy to patients at high risk of reconstruction failure (Expert Opinion).<sup>[[2]](#ref2)</sup>

finding: The long-bulbar row places all augmented anastomotic urethroplasty in Avoid, even though the cited HR concerns transecting AAU and EAU weakly recommends selected non-transecting augmented repair for a short, nearly obliterative segment.
evidence: PMID 32501135, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32501135/, opened abstract: retrospective comparison of 221 transecting AAU and 286 non-transecting dorsal onlay BMG repairs (507 included), mean follow-up 78.9 months, adjusted recurrence HR 4.8 using <16 Fr cystoscopic recurrence. EAU 2026 https://uroweb.org/guidelines/urethral-strictures/chapter/disease-management-in-males, §6.3.2.e.2, opened: weak recommendation for augmented non-transecting anastomotic repair in a short nearly obliterative segment.

edit.new: | Routine [transecting AAU](/docs/surgical-techniques/04a-urethral-reconstruction/augmented-anastomotic) when non-transecting graft repair is feasible (recurrence HR 4.8 versus non-transecting dorsal onlay in one retrospective cohort<sup>[[3]](#ref3)</sup>); a short nearly obliterative segment may warrant [non-transecting augmented repair](/docs/surgical-techniques/04a-urethral-reconstruction/ntaau) (EAU weak recommendation<sup>[[1]](#ref1)</sup>) |

finding: The fossa/meatal row makes a graft the primary operation for simple meatal stenosis. The initial meatotomy/meatoplasty decision and recurrent distal reconstruction decision need separate rows.
evidence: EAU 2026 https://uroweb.org/guidelines/urethral-strictures/chapter/disease-management-in-males, §6.3.1.f, opened: weak recommendation to offer open meatoplasty or distal urethroplasty for meatal/fossa disease. AUA 2023 unabridged local full text, statements 13–14, opened: initial dilation or meatotomy is permitted for uncomplicated meatal/fossa strictures; urethroplasty is offered for recurrent disease.

finding: The row equates a failed graft with an avascular recipient bed and steers every redo toward a skin flap. Prior graft failure alone does not rule out another oral-mucosal free graft, which EAU strongly recommends for a suitable long bulbar redo.
evidence: EAU 2026 https://uroweb.org/guidelines/urethral-strictures/chapter/disease-management-in-males, §6.3.2.h, opened: buccal free-graft redo series reported 82–86% patency; summary says redo free-graft patency can match primary cases and gives a strong recommendation for oral-mucosal free graft in long-stricture redo. EAU tissue-transfer chapter https://uroweb.org/guidelines/urethral-strictures/chapter/tissue-transfer, opened: flaps are a weakly recommended option when the bed has poor vascularity.

edit.old: | **Scarred bed / failed prior graft** | Pedicled flap ([Orandi](/docs/surgical-techniques/04a-urethral-reconstruction/orandi-flap), [McAninch](/docs/surgical-techniques/04a-urethral-reconstruction/mcaninch-circular-flap), [Quartey](/docs/surgical-techniques/04a-urethral-reconstruction/quartey-flap)) ± dorsal BMG | [Vanni / Zinman ventral BMG + gracilis](/docs/surgical-techniques/04a-urethral-reconstruction/vanni-zinman-ventral-bmg-gracilis) (radiation / salvage) | Free graft alone (poor bed) |
edit.new: | **Failed prior graft / compromised bed** | For a long bulbar redo with a viable bed, repeat [oral-mucosal free-graft urethroplasty](/docs/surgical-techniques/04a-urethral-reconstruction/dorsal-onlay-omg) (EAU strong)<sup>[[1]](#ref1)</sup>; for a truly poor bed with healthy non-LS genital skin, consider a pedicled flap ([Orandi](/docs/surgical-techniques/04a-urethral-reconstruction/orandi-flap), [McAninch](/docs/surgical-techniques/04a-urethral-reconstruction/mcaninch-circular-flap), [Quartey](/docs/surgical-techniques/04a-urethral-reconstruction/quartey-flap)) ± dorsal BMG | [Vanni / Zinman ventral BMG + gracilis](/docs/surgical-techniques/04a-urethral-reconstruction/vanni-zinman-ventral-bmg-gracilis) for radiation / salvage | An unsupported free graft in a poorly vascularized bed |

edit.old: The library spans >30 distinct techniques across 8 categories, evolving from the early staged approaches (Johanson 1953, Turner-Warwick 1960s) through the pedicled-flap era (Orandi 1968, Quartey 1983, McAninch 1993) to the BMG-dominant era (Barbagli 1996, Kulkarni 2009, Nikolavsky 2016) and an emerging minimally-invasive frontier (transmeatal, endoscopic, robotic, tissue-engineered).
edit.new: The database groups more than 30 procedures into eight categories. The linked techniques include staged repairs (Johanson 1953; Turner-Warwick 1960s), pedicled flaps (Orandi 1968; Quartey 1983; McAninch 1993), oral-mucosal graft repairs (Barbagli 1996; Kulkarni 2009; Nikolavsky 2016), and emerging transmeatal, endoscopic, robotic, and tissue-engineered approaches.

finding: The database files muscle-sparing urethroplasty under Anastomotic (no substitute tissue), although the linked technique spans graft repairs and EPA. A cross-cutting approach label would keep the taxonomy from implying that muscle sparing is itself an anastomotic repair.
evidence: EAU 2026 https://uroweb.org/guidelines/urethral-strictures/chapter/disease-management-in-males, §6.3.2.e.1, opened: the muscle- and nerve-sparing perineal approach is mostly used in graft urethroplasty but can also be used for EPA. Linked docs/04-surgical-techniques/04a-urethral-reconstruction/anastomotic/muscle-sparing-urethroplasty.mdx, opened, describes both graft and anastomotic applications.
